\paragraph{Statistical Comparison.} Following Dem\v{s}ar~\cite{demsar2006}, we apply the non-parametric Friedman test on macro-F1 ranks across the $N = 9$ datasets used in this paper, with $k = 8$ estimators. The Friedman statistic is $\chi^2_F = 12.33$ with $\mathrm{df} = 7$, indicating a significant overall difference in estimator performance under the usual $\alpha = 0.05$ threshold. We complement this with a post-hoc Nemenyi test, whose critical difference at $\alpha = 0.05$ is $\mathrm{CD} = 3.50$. Average ranks (lower is better):
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item HS: average rank 3.11
  \item ExSTraCS: average rank 3.56
  \item ruleGP: average rank 3.89
  \item rulePLCS: average rank 3.89
  \item ExSTraCS (LRC): average rank 4.67
  \item RuleKit: average rank 5.11
  \item ruleNLN: average rank 5.44
  \item ruleNSGA-II: average rank 6.33
\end{itemize}
Pairs whose average ranks differ by less than the critical difference and are therefore \emph{not} statistically distinguishable at $\alpha = 0.05$:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item HS -- ExSTraCS (rank difference 0.44 $<$ CD)
  \item HS -- ruleGP (rank difference 0.78 $<$ CD)
  \item HS -- rulePLCS (rank difference 0.78 $<$ CD)

  \item ExSTraCS -- ruleGP (rank difference 0.33 $<$ CD)

  \item ExSTraCS -- ruleNSGA-II (rank difference 2.78 $<$ CD)
  \item ruleGP -- rulePLCS (rank difference 0.00 $<$ CD)
